parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀκατάστατος (akatástatos, “unstable, irregular”), with semantic loan from French désordonné, en désordre, as well as semantic loan from German unordentlich.

parole.significato: halt, stop, don't move (order to stop moving)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French halte, from German halt. First attested 1876.
Learnedly from άνθρακ(ας) (ánthrak(as)) + -ούχος (-oúchos), a calque of French carbonifère and German kohlehaltig.
Learnedly from απο- (apo-) + δεσμεύω (desmévo), a calque of French dégager, désengager and German entbinden. Compare Ancient Greek ἀποδεσμεύω (apodesmeúō, “to bind fast”).
Borrowed from French benzine.

parole.significato: indicator, quotient, measure (something indicating a value)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek δείκτης (deíktēs, “who shows, points”) and semantic loan from French indice, indicateur and German Anzeiger, Anzeige. The sense "index finger" from Koine δεικτικός (deiktikós) by ellipsis of the noun δάκτυλος (dáktulos) ("the finger that points").
διεθνής (“international”) + -ισμός * (as theory): Calque of French internationalisme. Attested since 1893. * (linguistics): Calque of German Internationalismus.
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐπιβαρύνω (epibarúnō, “to press heavily on”) with semantic loan from French aggraver and German belasten. By surface analysis, επι- (epi-) + βαρύνω (varýno).

Learnedly, from Hellenistic Koine Greek ἐτυμολογία (etumología) from the ancient ἔτυμ(ος) (étum(os), “true”) + -ο- (-o-) + -λογία (-logía, “-logy”), semantic loan from French étymologie or German Etymologie from Latin etymologia.
Learned borrowing from French éosine or German Eosin, coined by Heinrich Caro from Ancient Greek ἠώς (ēṓs, “dawn”) + -in.

parole.testo: Learnedly from ιατρ(ός) (iatr(ós)) + -ο- (-o-) + δικαστής (dikastís), a calque of French médecin légiste or German Gerichtsarzt.
Learnedly from κράτ(ος) (krát(os)) + -ικός (-ikós), a calque of French étatique and German staatlich.
Learned borrowing from French critique & German Kritik, from Ancient Greek κριτική (τέχνη) (kritikḗ (tékhnē), “art of judging”), substantivised feminine of adjective κριτικός (kritikós).
Free translation of French calque (phraséologique), or a calque of German Lehnübersetzung or English loan translation. See σημασιολογικό δάνειο (simasiologikó dáneio, “semantic loan”).

Learned formation from ομιλώ (omiló) + -τής (-tís), with semantic loan from French orateur and semantic loan from German Redner. Related to, but not derived from, the phonetically identical Ancient Greek ὁμιλητής (homilētḗs, “disciple”).
Learnedly from όπλο (óplo, “weapon”) + κατοχή (katochí, “possession”), a calque of French détention d'armes or German Waffenbesitz.

Learnedly, from Ancient Greek παράδοσις (parádosis) + modern ending -ση (-si), thus παρά- (pará-) + δόση f (dósi, “dose, portion, gift”). parole.significato: mesh, lattice, network, braid (a structure made of connected strands)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek πλέγμα (plégma) with semantic loan from French réseau (“network”) and German Komplex (“complex”).
Learnedly from πρωτο- (proto-) + -δικείο (-dikeío), a calque of French tribunal de première instance or German Gericht erster Instanz.

parole.significato: session, sitting, meeting (of a committee, council, etc. to conduct business)
parole.testo: Learnedly from συνεδριάζω (synedriázo) + -ση (-si), a calque of French séance and German Sitzung.

Learned borrowing from Koine Greek ὑπεράνθρωπος (huperánthrōpos, “superior to man”) with semantic loan from French surhumain and German Übermensch. By surface analysis, υπερ- (yper-) + άνθρωπος (ánthropos).
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ὑψίπεδον (hupsípedon), neuter of ὑψίπεδος (hupsípedos, adjective), with semantic loan from French haut plateau and German Hochebene.
From χειρ (cheir, “hand”) + -ό- (-ó-) + φρένο (fréno, “brake”)., calque of French frein à main or German Handbremse.
